name: ethora
description: Build and run chat apps, messaging rooms and AI agents on Ethora from ChatGPT: create an app, open rooms, add users, create agents with a knowledge base, put a chat widget on a website.

interface.longDescription:
Ethora is an open-source chat and messaging platform with a built-in AI agent framework. This plugin connects ChatGPT to your Ethora account so you can build and run chat products by describing them.

What you can do:
- Create a chat app (your own tenant with users, rooms and branding) and open chat rooms.
- Create AI agents with a persona and a knowledge base from a website or uploaded documents, put them in rooms, and talk to them.
- Seed a room with several agents that reply to people and to each other.
- Generate the <script> tag that puts an AI chat widget on any website.
- Send and read messages, search message history, manage users and files.

Who it is for: product teams and developers adding chat or AI assistants to a website or app, and anyone who wants a working chat space with AI participants without setting up infrastructure.

How it works: you sign in with your Ethora account (or create one in the conversation). Tools act only on apps you own. A compact core tool set is listed by default; more tools are enabled on request within the conversation.

Data: the plugin works with the account, apps, rooms, users, agents, files and messages you create on Ethora, under the Ethora privacy policy. It does not ask for, and must not be used to collect, health or medical information, government identifiers, payment card numbers, biometric data or other sensitive personal data.

Limitations: the plugin manages apps, rooms, users and agents. It does not render chat inside ChatGPT; people chat in the Ethora web client, your app via the chat component, or the website widget. Webhooks, push-notification setup, moderation actions and billing are managed in the Ethora dashboard, not through the plugin. Wallet and crypto features are not available in the hosted server.
capabilities: Create a chat app with rooms and users
Create AI agents with a persona and a knowledge base
Put several AI agents in one room that talk to people and each other
Generate a chat widget embed for any website
Send and read messages, search chat history
Crawl a website or upload documents as agent knowledge
Manage API keys and app tokens for integrations
defaultPrompt: Create an Ethora app called Support Desk with a room and an AI agent that answers from our docs.
Put a chat widget on my website that answers questions about our product.
Set up a room with two AI agents who debate a topic with me.

positive.description: Create a new chat app and make it the current app.
positive.prompt: Create an Ethora app called Review Desk.
positive.expected_behavior: The assistant creates the app and reports its name and id from `created`, offers the `next` steps (select the app, create a room, create an agent) and does not ask for any credential.

positive.description: Create a room and post a message to it.
positive.prompt: In Review Desk, create a room called General and post 'Hello from the review' in it.
positive.expected_behavior: A room is created (its JID comes back in `created.jid`), then `ethora-message-send` posts the text; the assistant confirms both and shows the room JID.

positive.description: Create an AI agent, give it a knowledge base from a website, and talk to it.
positive.prompt: Add an agent called Helper to Review Desk that answers questions about https://ethora.com, invite it to General, and ask it what Ethora is.
positive.expected_behavior: The agent is created, `ethora-source-site-crawl-wait` indexes the site, `ethora-agent-invite` puts it in the room, `ethora-message-send` with waitForReplySec returns the agent's answer in `replies` with `senderName: Helper`.

positive.description: Generate the website chat widget embed.
positive.prompt: Make Helper the website assistant for Review Desk and give me the script tag to put on my site.
positive.expected_behavior: `ethora-agent-activate` binds the agent as the app's widget bot, then `ethora-widget-snippet-get` returns a `<script>` tag; the assistant shows the snippet and the prerequisites.

positive.description: Read recent messages with named senders.
positive.prompt: Show me the last messages in General and who sent them.
positive.expected_behavior: History rows come back with `senderName` and `senderKind`; the assistant lists them as 'Helper: ...', 'app: ...' rather than raw ids.

negative.description: The plugin should not be invoked. The user wants code for their own chat server, not an action on their Ethora account; the model should write the code without calling any Ethora tool. Expected: no tool call.
negative.prompt: Write a Python script that implements a simple WebSocket chat server with rooms.

negative.description: The plugin should not be invoked. A comparison of third-party chat products is general knowledge; nothing is created, read or changed on Ethora. Expected: no tool call.
negative.prompt: What are the main differences between Slack and Microsoft Teams for a 50-person company?

negative.description: The plugin should not be invoked. An explanation of retrieval-augmented generation is a concept question; the plugin's knowledge-base tools only apply when the user asks to build or feed an agent. Expected: no tool call.
negative.prompt: Explain how retrieval-augmented generation works and when I should use it instead of fine-tuning.

publication.release_notes: 26.10.1: every tool sets readOnlyHint, destructiveHint, idempotentHint and openWorldHint explicitly, from a reviewed table with a stated reason per tool (docs/TOOL_ANNOTATIONS.md in the repository). The agent-flows guidance uses a demo-request example and states that flows and tools are for contact and business details only, never health, government-id, payment-card or biometric data. New since 26.10.0: scheduled website re-crawl tools, widget appearance tools, agent try and knowledge-health tools, remembered app selection across sessions.
